sources.citation: Campbell, Lyle, Nala Huiying Lee, Eve Okura, Sean Simpson & Kaori Ueki. 2022. Catalogue of Endangered Languages (ELCat) entry 'Kendeje' (endangeredlanguages.com/lang/klf).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2021. The Maban languages and their place within Nilo-Saharan. Draft circulated for discussion, Cambridge, 10 January 2021, 25 pp. (via web.archive.org copy of rogerblench.info)
sources.note: Nothing for Kendeje. Kendeje appears only in Table 1 (name, location, 1,860 speakers, dialects Yaali/Faranga) and the tree; sec. 2.3 states 'Our only knowledge of some varieties appears to be from SIL Survey reports, mostly unpublished, and not always including the data on which the conclusions are based (e.g. Maass, Grant & Prinz 1995, 1996..)'. Sec. 4.3 'Tones' covers Maba (H, L, R, F per Weiss 2009) and Aiki (two heights) only; no stress discussion; comparative wordlist (Table 13, from Edgar 1991b) has no Kendeje column.

sources.note: Lists only Ethnologue, Glottolog, LINGUIST List pages and the 1996 SIL survey (sil.org archive ids 4838 and 50809). No language description of any kind.

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2019. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 22nd edition. Entry 'Kendeje' [klf]. Dallas: SIL International. (Read from the the Internet Archive capture of 2019-06-06; the 2016 capture of the 19th edition was also read and is identical minus the Writing line.)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content. The entry has no Typology line and no Language Development section; it gives population 1,860 (2000), EGIDS 7 (Shifting), dialects Yaali/Faranga with 89% lexical similarity, L2 use of Maba and Masalit, and 'Writing: Unwritten [Qaax]'. This confirms that no SIL orthography statement or phonology sketch (which would carry a tone/stress note) had been produced as of 2019.

sources.note: Only the 1996 survey report (two archive records). No orthography statement, phonology sketch or grammar listed.

sources.citation: Weiss, Doris. 2009. Phonologie et morphosyntaxe du maba. Thèse de doctorat, Université Lumière Lyon 2. 461 pp. (HAL tel-01540280)
sources.note: Describes MABA (maba1277), the closest documented relative, not Kendeje; the word 'kendeje/kendedje/yaali/faranga' does not occur in the thesis. For Maba, sec. 2.2.1 'Accent tonique' (pp. 43-45): intensity accent is non-distinctive and predictable from tone height (every H syllable stressed), vowel length (long vowels stressed) and word shape; tone is distinctive. Not usable as a Kendeje statement.

Berlin / New York: Mouton de Gruyter. xvii+454 pp. [copies we hold is the complete volume; African chapters read: ch. 6 Brenzinger 'Language Endangerment in Northern Africa' 123–139; ch. 7 Blench 'Endangered Languages in West Africa' 140–162; ch. 8 Connell 'Endangered Languages in Central Africa' 163–178; ch. 9 Brenzinger 'Language Endangerment in Southern and Eastern Africa' 179–204]
sources.note: Nothing on stress/tone: table row only — 'Only in the home; Maba and Masalit used outside'.

sources.citation: Connell, Bruce. 2007. Endangered languages in Central Africa. In Matthias Brenzinger (ed.), Language Diversity Endangered (Trends in Linguistics. Studies and Monographs 181), 163-178. Berlin/New York: Mouton de Gruyter. doi:10.1515/9783110197129.163
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: nothing; sociolinguistic table row only ('< 2,000 | Only in the home; Maba and Masalit used outside'). The same table lists Massalat (row 45, p. 176, '10' speakers) - Connell 2007 is already among Massalat's works seen. No other target language of the group is named anywhere in the volume (a full-text search for stress/accent: Surbakhal, Marfa, Karanga, Kodoi, Mimi absent).

sources.citation: Maass, Antje, Angela Prinz & Caroline Grant. 1996. Rapport d'enquête sociolinguistique: première évaluation parmi les Kendedje du Ouaddaï. N'Djaména: Association SIL. ii+12 pp. (SIL archive 50809; downloaded via web.archive.org snapshot of the sil.org PDF)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic first-assessment survey (fieldwork 26-27 Jan 1995): classification by lexicostatistics (Kendeje 69-71% with Maba, 59-64% with Masalit), bilingualism, vitality. No phonology; wordlists collected but not printed (only the similarity table, App. B). States (sec. 1.2) that Kendeje was until then 'un parler jusqu'à présent inconnu au monde académique'.

sources.citation: Maass, Antje, Caroline Grant & Angela Prinz. 1995-1996. Unpublished Kendeje-Yaali and Kendeje-Faranga survey wordlists (WordSurv database) underlying the 1996 Rapport d'enquête; Association SIL Tchad archives, N'Djaména.
